summary: Trust maps can become stale compliance theater, and provider-level labels may hide service-, region- and configuration-specific differences.

points.text: A provider marked trusted can still expose an unsafe endpoint, subprocessor, region or retention setting; coarse provider labels create dangerous transitive trust.
Public certifications and questionnaires are lagging evidence and may not cover the exact service configuration or emerging failure mode used by an agent.
A large task-by-data-by-provider matrix is expensive to maintain and can lead teams to route around controls when legitimate combinations are missing.
Self-hosting reduces some contractual exposure but shifts patching, access-control and incident-response risk to the deploying organization; it is not automatically the highest-trust route.
